# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

13	class BasePoints:
14	    """Base class for Points.
15	
16	    Args:
17	        tensor (Tensor or np.ndarray or Sequence[Sequence[float]]): The points
18	            data with shape (N, points_dim).
19	        points_dim (int): Integer indicating the dimension of a point. Each row
20	            is (x, y, z, ...). Defaults to 3.
21	        attribute_dims (dict, optional): Dictionary to indicate the meaning of
22	            extra dimension. Defaults to None.
23	
24	    Attributes:
25	        tensor (Tensor): Float matrix with shape (N, points_dim).
26	        points_dim (int): Integer indicating the dimension of a point. Each row
27	            is (x, y, z, ...).
28	        attribute_dims (dict, optional): Dictionary to indicate the meaning of
29	            extra dimension. Defaults to None.
30	        rotation_axis (int): Default rotation axis for points rotation.
31	    """
32	
33	    def __init__(self,
34	                 tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray, Sequence[Sequence[float]]],
35	                 points_dim: int = 3,
36	                 attribute_dims: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
37	        if isinstance(tensor, Tensor):
38	            device = tensor.device
39	        else:
40	            device = torch.device('cpu')
41	        tensor = torch.as_tensor(tensor, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
42	        if tensor.numel() == 0:
43	            # Use reshape, so we don't end up creating a new tensor that does
44	            # not depend on the inputs (and consequently confuses jit)
45	            tensor = tensor.reshape((-1, points_dim))
46	        assert tensor.dim() == 2 and tensor.size(-1) == points_dim, \
47	            ('The points dimension must be 2 and the length of the last '
48	             f'dimension must be {points_dim}, but got points with shape '
49	             f'{tensor.shape}.')
50	
51	        self.tensor = tensor.clone()
52	        self.points_dim = points_dim
53	        self.attribute_dims = attribute_dims
54	        self.rotation_axis = 0
55	
56	    @property
57	    def coord(self) -> Tensor:
58	        """Tensor: Coordinates of each point in shape (N, 3)."""
59	        return self.tensor[:, :3]
60	
61	    @coord.setter
62	    def coord(self, tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray]) -> None:
63	        """Set the coordinates of each point.
64	
65	        Args:
66	            tensor (Tensor or np.ndarray): Coordinates of each point with shape
67	                (N, 3).
68	        """
69	        try:
70	            tensor = tensor.reshape(self.shape[0], 3)
71	        except (RuntimeError, ValueError):  # for torch.Tensor and np.ndarray
72	            raise ValueError(f'got unexpected shape {tensor.shape}')
73	        if not isinstance(tensor, Tensor):
74	            tensor = self.tensor.new_tensor(tensor)
75	        self.tensor[:, :3] = tensor
76	
77	    @property
78	    def height(self) -> Union[Tensor, None]:
79	        """Tensor or None: Returns a vector with height of each point in shape
80	        (N, )."""
81	        if self.attribute_dims is not None and \
82	                'height' in self.attribute_dims.keys():
83	            return self.tensor[:, self.attribute_dims['height']]
84	        else:
85	            return None
86	
87	    @height.setter
88	    def height(self, tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray]) -> None:
89	        """Set the height of each point.
90	
91	        Args:
92	            tensor (Tensor or np.ndarray): Height of each point with shape
93	                (N, ).
94	        """
95	        try:
96	            tensor = tensor.reshape(self.shape[0])
97	        except (RuntimeError, ValueError):  # for torch.Tensor and np.ndarray
98	            raise ValueError(f'got unexpected shape {tensor.shape}')
99	        if not isinstance(tensor, Tensor):
100	            tensor = self.tensor.new_tensor(tensor)
101	        if self.attribute_dims is not None and \
102	                'height' in self.attribute_dims.keys():
103	            self.tensor[:, self.attribute_dims['height']] = tensor
104	        else:
105	            # add height attribute
106	            if self.attribute_dims is None:
107	                self.attribute_dims = dict()
108	            attr_dim = self.shape[1]
109	            self.tensor = torch.cat([self.tensor, tensor.unsqueeze(1)], dim=1)
110	            self.attribute_dims.update(dict(height=attr_dim))
111	            self.points_dim += 1
112	
113	    @property
114	    def color(self) -> Union[Tensor, None]:
115	        """Tensor or None: Returns a vector with color of each point in shape
116	        (N, 3)."""
117	        if self.attribute_dims is not None and \
118	                'color' in self.attribute_dims.keys():
119	            return self.tensor[:, self.attribute_dims['color']]
120	        else:
121	            return None
122	
123	    @color.setter
124	    def color(self, tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray]) -> None:
125	        """Set the color of each point.
126	
127	        Args:
128	            tensor (Tensor or np.ndarray): Color of each point with shape
129	                (N, 3).
130	        """
131	        try:
132	            tensor = tensor.reshape(self.shape[0], 3)
133	        except (RuntimeError, ValueError):  # for torch.Tensor and np.ndarray
134	            raise ValueError(f'got unexpected shape {tensor.shape}')
135	        if tensor.max() >= 256 or tensor.min() < 0:
136	            warnings.warn('point got color value beyond [0, 255]')
137	        if not isinstance(tensor, Tensor):
138	            tensor = self.tensor.new_tensor(tensor)
139	        if self.attribute_dims is not None and \
140	                'color' in self.attribute_dims.keys():
141	            self.tensor[:, self.attribute_dims['color']] = tensor
142	        else:
143	            # add color attribute
144	            if self.attribute_dims is None:
145	                self.attribute_dims = dict()
146	            attr_dim = self.shape[1]
147	            self.tensor = torch.cat([self.tensor, tensor], dim=1)
148	            self.attribute_dims.update(
149	                dict(color=[attr_dim, attr_dim + 1, attr_dim + 2]))
150	            self.points_dim += 3
151	
152	    @property
153	    def shape(self) -> torch.Size:
154	        """torch.Size: Shape of points."""
155	        return self.tensor.shape
156	
157	    def shuffle(self) -> Tensor:
158	        """Shuffle the points.
159	
160	        Returns:
161	            Tensor: The shuffled index.
162	        """
163	        idx = torch.randperm(self.__len__(), device=self.tensor.device)
164	        self.tensor = self.tensor[idx]
165	        return idx
166	
167	    def rotate(self,
168	               rotation: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray, float],
169	               axis: Optional[int] = None) -> Tensor:
170	        """Rotate points with the given rotation matrix or angle.
171	
172	        Args:
173	            rotation (Tensor or np.ndarray or float): Rotation matrix or angle.
174	            axis (int, optional): Axis to rotate at. Defaults to None.
175	
176	        Returns:
177	            Tensor: Rotation matrix.
178	        """
179	        if not isinstance(rotation, Tensor):
180	            rotation = self.tensor.new_tensor(rotation)
181	        assert rotation.shape == torch.Size([3, 3]) or rotation.numel() == 1, \
182	            f'invalid rotation shape {rotation.shape}'
183	
184	        if axis is None:
185	            axis = self.rotation_axis
186	
187	        if rotation.numel() == 1:
188	            rotated_points, rot_mat_T = rotation_3d_in_axis(
189	                self.tensor[:, :3][None], rotation, axis=axis, return_mat=True)
190	            self.tensor[:, :3] = rotated_points.squeeze(0)
191	            rot_mat_T = rot_mat_T.squeeze(0)
192	        else:
193	            # rotation.numel() == 9
194	            self.tensor[:, :3] = self.tensor[:, :3] @ rotation
195	            rot_mat_T = rotation
196	
197	        return rot_mat_T
198	
199	    @abstractmethod
200	    def flip(self, bev_direction: str = 'horizontal') -> None:
201	        """Flip the points along given BEV direction.
202	
203	        Args:
204	            bev_direction (str): Flip direction (horizontal or vertical).
205	                Defaults to 'horizontal'.
206	        """
207	        pass
208	
209	    def translate(self, trans_vector: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray]) -> None:
210	        """Translate points with the given translation vector.
211	
212	        Args:
213	            trans_vector (Tensor or np.ndarray): Translation vector of size 3
214	                or nx3.
215	        """
216	        if not isinstance(trans_vector, Tensor):
217	            trans_vector = self.tensor.new_tensor(trans_vector)
218	        trans_vector = trans_vector.squeeze(0)
219	        if trans_vector.dim() == 1:
220	            assert trans_vector.shape[0] == 3
221	        elif trans_vector.dim() == 2:
222	            assert trans_vector.shape[0] == self.tensor.shape[0] and \
223	                trans_vector.shape[1] == 3
224	        else:
225	            raise NotImplementedError(
226	                f'Unsupported translation vector of shape {trans_vector.shape}'
227	            )
228	        self.tensor[:, :3] += trans_vector

230	    def in_range_3d(
231	            self, point_range: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray,
232	                                     Sequence[float]]) -> Tensor:
233	        """Check whether the points are in the given range.
234	
235	        Args:
236	            point_range (Tensor or np.ndarray or Sequence[float]): The range of
237	                point (x_min, y_min, z_min, x_max, y_max, z_max).
238	
239	        Note:
240	            In the original implementation of SECOND, checking whether a box in
241	            the range checks whether the points are in a convex polygon, we try
242	            to reduce the burden for simpler cases.
243	
244	        Returns:
245	            Tensor: A binary vector indicating whether each point is inside the
246	            reference range.
247	        """
248	        in_range_flags = ((self.tensor[:, 0] > point_range[0])
249	                          & (self.tensor[:, 1] > point_range[1])
250	                          & (self.tensor[:, 2] > point_range[2])
251	                          & (self.tensor[:, 0] < point_range[3])
252	                          & (self.tensor[:, 1] < point_range[4])
253	                          & (self.tensor[:, 2] < point_range[5]))
254	        return in_range_flags
255	
256	    @property
257	    def bev(self) -> Tensor:
258	        """Tensor: BEV of the points in shape (N, 2)."""
259	        return self.tensor[:, [0, 1]]
260	
261	    def in_range_bev(
262	            self, point_range: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray,
263	                                     Sequence[float]]) -> Tensor:
264	        """Check whether the points are in the given range.
265	
266	        Args:
267	            point_range (Tensor or np.ndarray or Sequence[float]): The range of
268	                point in order of (x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max).
269	
270	        Returns:
271	            Tensor: A binary vector indicating whether each point is inside the
272	            reference range.
273	        """
274	        in_range_flags = ((self.bev[:, 0] > point_range[0])
275	                          & (self.bev[:, 1] > point_range[1])
276	                          & (self.bev[:, 0] < point_range[2])
277	                          & (self.bev[:, 1] < point_range[3]))
278	        return in_range_flags
279	
280	    @abstractmethod
281	    def convert_to(self,
282	                   dst: int,
283	                   rt_mat: Optional[Union[Tensor,
284	                                          np.ndarray]] = None) -> 'BasePoints':
285	        """Convert self to ``dst`` mode.
286	
287	        Args:
288	            dst (int): The target Point mode.
289	            rt_mat (Tensor or np.ndarray, optional): The rotation and
290	                translation matrix between different coordinates.
291	                Defaults to None. The conversion from ``src`` coordinates to
292	                ``dst`` coordinates usually comes along the change of sensors,
293	                e.g., from camera to LiDAR. This requires a transformation
294	                matrix.
295	
296	        Returns:
297	            :obj:`BasePoints`: The converted point of the same type in the
298	            ``dst`` mode.
299	        """
300	        pass
301	
302	    def scale(self, scale_factor: float) -> None:
303	        """Scale the points with horizontal and vertical scaling factors.
304	
305	        Args:
306	            scale_factors (float): Scale factors to scale the points.
307	        """
308	        self.tensor[:, :3] *= scale_factor
309	
310	    def __getitem__(
311	            self, item: Union[int, tuple, slice, np.ndarray,
312	                              Tensor]) -> 'BasePoints':
313	        """
314	        Args:
315	            item (int or tuple or slice or np.ndarray or Tensor): Index of
316	                points.
317	
318	        Note:
319	            The following usage are allowed:
320	
321	            1. `new_points = points[3]`: Return a `Points` that contains only
322	               one point.
323	            2. `new_points = points[2:10]`: Return a slice of points.
324	            3. `new_points = points[vector]`: Whether vector is a
325	               torch.BoolTensor with `length = len(points)`. Nonzero elements
326	               in the vector will be selected.
327	            4. `new_points = points[3:11, vector]`: Return a slice of points
328	               and attribute dims.
329	            5. `new_points = points[4:12, 2]`: Return a slice of points with
330	               single attribute.
331	
332	            Note that the returned Points might share storage with this Points,
333	            subject to PyTorch's indexing semantics.
334	
335	        Returns:
336	            :obj:`BasePoints`: A new object of :class:`BasePoints` after
337	            indexing.
338	        """
339	        original_type = type(self)
340	        if isinstance(item, int):
341	            return original_type(
342	                self.tensor[item].view(1, -1),
343	                points_dim=self.points_dim,
344	                attribute_dims=self.attribute_dims)
345	        elif isinstance(item, tuple) and len(item) == 2:
346	            if isinstance(item[1], slice):
347	                start = 0 if item[1].start is None else item[1].start
348	                stop = self.tensor.shape[1] \
349	                    if item[1].stop is None else item[1].stop
350	                step = 1 if item[1].step is None else item[1].step
351	                item = list(item)
352	                item[1] = list(range(start, stop, step))
353	                item = tuple(item)
354	            elif isinstance(item[1], int):
355	                item = list(item)
356	                item[1] = [item[1]]
357	                item = tuple(item)
358	            p = self.tensor[item[0], item[1]]
359	
360	            keep_dims = list(
361	                set(item[1]).intersection(set(range(3, self.tensor.shape[1]))))
362	            if self.attribute_dims is not None:
363	                attribute_dims = self.attribute_dims.copy()
364	                for key in self.attribute_dims.keys():
365	                    cur_attribute_dims = attribute_dims[key]
366	                    if isinstance(cur_attribute_dims, int):
367	                        cur_attribute_dims = [cur_attribute_dims]
368	                    intersect_attr = list(
369	                        set(cur_attribute_dims).intersection(set(keep_dims)))
370	                    if len(intersect_attr) == 1:
371	                        attribute_dims[key] = intersect_attr[0]
372	                    elif len(intersect_attr) > 1:
373	                        attribute_dims[key] = intersect_attr
374	                    else:
375	                        attribute_dims.pop(key)
376	            else:
377	                attribute_dims = None
378	        elif isinstance(item, (slice, np.ndarray, Tensor)):
379	            p = self.tensor[item]
380	            attribute_dims = self.attribute_dims
381	        else:
382	            raise NotImplementedError(f'Invalid slice {item}!')
383	
384	        assert p.dim() == 2, \
385	            f'Indexing on Points with {item} failed to return a matrix!'
386	        return original_type(
387	            p, points_dim=p.shape[1], attribute_dims=attribute_dims)

389	    def __len__(self) -> int:
390	        """int: Number of points in the current object."""
391	        return self.tensor.shape[0]
392	
393	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
394	        """str: Return a string that describes the object."""

397	    @classmethod
398	    def cat(cls, points_list: Sequence['BasePoints']) -> 'BasePoints':
399	        """Concatenate a list of Points into a single Points.
400	
401	        Args:
402	            points_list (Sequence[:obj:`BasePoints`]): List of points.
403	
404	        Returns:
405	            :obj:`BasePoints`: The concatenated points.
406	        """
407	        assert isinstance(points_list, (list, tuple))
408	        if len(points_list) == 0:
409	            return cls(torch.empty(0))
410	        assert all(isinstance(points, cls) for points in points_list)
411	
412	        # use torch.cat (v.s. layers.cat)
413	        # so the returned points never share storage with input
414	        cat_points = cls(
415	            torch.cat([p.tensor for p in points_list], dim=0),
416	            points_dim=points_list[0].points_dim,
417	            attribute_dims=points_list[0].attribute_dims)
418	        return cat_points

443	        Returns:

501	    def new_point(
502	        self, data: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray, Sequence[Sequence[float]]]
503	    ) -> 'BasePoints':
504	        """Create a new point object with data.
505	
506	        The new point and its tensor has the similar properties as self and
507	        self.tensor, respectively.
508	
509	        Args:
510	            data (Tensor or np.ndarray or Sequence[Sequence[float]]): Data to
511	                be copied.
512	
513	        Returns:
514	            :obj:`BasePoints`: A new point object with ``data``, the object's
515	            other properties are similar to ``self``.
516	        """
517	        new_tensor = self.tensor.new_tensor(data) \
518	            if not isinstance(data, Tensor) else data.to(self.device)
519	        original_type = type(self)
520	        return original_type(
521	            new_tensor,
522	            points_dim=self.points_dim,

from typing import Optional, Sequence, Union

import numpy as np
from torch import Tensor

from .base_points import BasePoints


class CameraPoints(BasePoints):
    """Points of instances in CAM coordinates.

    Args:
        tensor (Tensor or np.ndarray or Sequence[Sequence[float]]): The points
            data with shape (N, points_dim).
        points_dim (int): Integer indicating the dimension of a point. Each row
            is (x, y, z, ...). Defaults to 3.
        attribute_dims (dict, optional): Dictionary to indicate the meaning of
            extra dimension. Defaults to None.

    Attributes:
        tensor (Tensor): Float matrix with shape (N, points_dim).
        points_dim (int): Integer indicating the dimension of a point. Each row
            is (x, y, z, ...).
        attribute_dims (dict, optional): Dictionary to indicate the meaning of
            extra dimension. Defaults to None.
        rotation_axis (int): Default rotation axis for points rotation.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 tensor: Union[Tensor, np.ndarray, Sequence[Sequence[float]]],
                 points_dim: int = 3,
                 attribute_dims: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
        super(CameraPoints, self).__init__(
            tensor, points_dim=points_dim, attribute_dims=attribute_dims)
        self.rotation_axis = 1

    def flip(self, bev_direction: str = 'horizontal') -> None:
        """Flip the points along given BEV direction.

        Args:
            bev_direction (str): Flip direction (horizontal or vertical).
                Defaults to 'horizontal'.
        """
        assert bev_direction in ('horizontal', 'vertical')
        if bev_direction == 'horizontal':
            self.tensor[:, 0] = -self.tensor[:, 0]
        elif bev_direction == 'vertical':
            self.tensor[:, 2] = -self.tensor[:, 2]

    @property
    def bev(self) -> Tensor:
        """Tensor: BEV of the points in shape (N, 2)."""
        return self.tensor[:, [0, 2]]

    def convert_to(self,
                   dst: int,
                   rt_mat: Optional[Union[Tensor,
                                          np.ndarray]] = None) -> 'BasePoints':
        """Convert self to ``dst`` mode.

        Args:
            dst (int): The target Point mode.
            rt_mat (Tensor or np.ndarray, optional): The rotation and
                translation matrix between different coordinates.
                Defaults to None. The conversion from ``src`` coordinates to
                ``dst`` coordinates usually comes along the change of sensors,
                e.g., from camera to LiDAR. This requires a transformation
                matrix.

        Returns:
            :obj:`BasePoints`: The converted point of the same type in the
            ``dst`` mode.
        """
        from mmdet3d.structures.bbox_3d import Coord3DMode
        return Coord3DMode.convert_point(
            point=self, src=Coord3DMode.CAM, dst=dst, rt_mat=rt_mat)

from .base_points import BasePoints
from .cam_points import CameraPoints
from .depth_points import DepthPoints
from .lidar_points import LiDARPoints

__all__ = ['BasePoints', 'CameraPoints', 'DepthPoints', 'LiDARPoints']


def get_points_type(points_type: str) -> type:
    """Get the class of points according to coordinate type.

    Args:
        points_type (str): The type of points coordinate. The valid value are
            "CAMERA", "LIDAR" and "DEPTH".

    Returns:
        type: Points type.
    """
    points_type_upper = points_type.upper()
    if points_type_upper == 'CAMERA':
        points_cls = CameraPoints
    elif points_type_upper == 'LIDAR':
        points_cls = LiDARPoints
    elif points_type_upper == 'DEPTH':
        points_cls = DepthPoints
    else:
        raise ValueError('Only "points_type" of "CAMERA", "LIDAR" and "DEPTH" '
                         f'are supported, got {points_type}')

    return points_cls

# Copyright (c) OpenMMLab. All rights reserved.
from enum import IntEnum, unique
from typing import Optional, Sequence, Union

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import Tensor

from mmdet3d.structures.points import (BasePoints, CameraPoints, DepthPoints,
                                       LiDARPoints)
from .base_box3d import BaseInstance3DBoxes
from .box_3d_mode import Box3DMode


@unique
class Coord3DMode(IntEnum):
    """Enum of different ways to represent a box and point cloud.

    Coordinates in LiDAR:

    .. code-block:: none

                    up z
                       ^   x front
                       |  /
                       | /
        left y <------ 0

    The relative coordinate of bottom center in a LiDAR box is (0.5, 0.5, 0),
    and the yaw is around the z axis, thus the rotation axis=2.

    Coordinates in Camera:

    .. code-block:: none

                z front
               /
              /
             0 ------> x right
             |
             |
             v
        down y

    The relative coordinate of bottom center in a CAM box is (0.5, 1.0, 0.5),
    and the yaw is around the y axis, thus the rotation axis=1.

    Coordinates in Depth:

    .. code-block:: none

        up z
           ^   y front
           |  /
           | /
           0 ------> x right

    The relative coordinate of bottom center in a DEPTH box is (0.5, 0.5, 0),
    and the yaw is around the z axis, thus the rotation axis=2.
    """

    LIDAR = 0
    CAM = 1
    DEPTH = 2

    @staticmethod
    def convert(input: Union[Sequence[float], np.ndarray, Tensor,
                             BaseInstance3DBoxes, BasePoints],
                src: Union[Box3DMode, 'Coord3DMode'],
                dst: Union[Box3DMode, 'Coord3DMode'],
                rt_mat: Optional[Union[np.ndarray, Tensor]] = None,
                with_yaw: bool = True,
                correct_yaw: bool = False,
                is_point: bool = True):
        """Convert boxes or points from ``src`` mode to ``dst`` mode.

        Args:
            input (Sequence[float] or np.ndarray or Tensor or
                :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes` or :obj:`BasePoints`): Can be a
                k-tuple, k-list or an Nxk array/tensor.
            src (:obj:`Box3DMode` or :obj:`Coord3DMode`): The source mode.
            dst (:obj:`Box3DMode` or :obj:`Coord3DMode`): The target mode.
            rt_mat (np.ndarray or Tensor, optional): The rotation and
                translation matrix between different coordinates.
                Defaults to None. The conversion from ``src`` coordinates to
                ``dst`` coordinates usually comes along the change of sensors,
                e.g., from camera to LiDAR. This requires a transformation
                matrix.
            with_yaw (bool): If ``box`` is an instance of
                :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes`, whether or not it has a yaw angle.
                Defaults to True.
            correct_yaw (bool): If the yaw is rotated by rt_mat.
                Defaults to False.
            is_point (bool): If ``input`` is neither an instance of
                :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes` nor an instance of
                :obj:`BasePoints`, whether or not it is point data.
                Defaults to True.

        Returns:
            Sequence[float] or np.ndarray or Tensor or
            :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes` or :obj:`BasePoints`: The converted box
            or points of the same type.
        """
        if isinstance(input, BaseInstance3DBoxes):
            return Coord3DMode.convert_box(
                input,
                src,
                dst,
                rt_mat=rt_mat,
                with_yaw=with_yaw,
                correct_yaw=correct_yaw)
        elif isinstance(input, BasePoints):
            return Coord3DMode.convert_point(input, src, dst, rt_mat=rt_mat)
        elif isinstance(input, (tuple, list, np.ndarray, Tensor)):
            if is_point:
                return Coord3DMode.convert_point(
                    input, src, dst, rt_mat=rt_mat)
            else:
                return Coord3DMode.convert_box(
                    input,
                    src,
                    dst,
                    rt_mat=rt_mat,
                    with_yaw=with_yaw,
                    correct_yaw=correct_yaw)
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError

    @staticmethod
    def convert_box(
        box: Union[Sequence[float], np.ndarray, Tensor, BaseInstance3DBoxes],
        src: Box3DMode,
        dst: Box3DMode,
        rt_mat: Optional[Union[np.ndarray, Tensor]] = None,
        with_yaw: bool = True,
        correct_yaw: bool = False
    ) -> Union[Sequence[float], np.ndarray, Tensor, BaseInstance3DBoxes]:
        """Convert boxes from ``src`` mode to ``dst`` mode.

        Args:
            box (Sequence[float] or np.ndarray or Tensor or
                :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes`): Can be a k-tuple, k-list or an Nxk
                array/tensor.
            src (:obj:`Box3DMode`): The source box mode.
            dst (:obj:`Box3DMode`): The target box mode.
            rt_mat (np.ndarray or Tensor, optional): The rotation and
                translation matrix between different coordinates.
                Defaults to None. The conversion from ``src`` coordinates to
                ``dst`` coordinates usually comes along the change of sensors,
                e.g., from camera to LiDAR. This requires a transformation
                matrix.
            with_yaw (bool): If ``box`` is an instance of
                :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes`, whether or not it has a yaw angle.
                Defaults to True.
            correct_yaw (bool): If the yaw is rotated by rt_mat.
                Defaults to False.

        Returns:
            Sequence[float] or np.ndarray or Tensor or
            :obj:`BaseInstance3DBoxes`: The converted box of the same type.
        """
        return Box3DMode.convert(
            box,
            src,
            dst,
            rt_mat=rt_mat,
            with_yaw=with_yaw,
            correct_yaw=correct_yaw)

    @staticmethod
    def convert_point(
        point: Union[Sequence[float], np.ndarray, Tensor, BasePoints],
        src: 'Coord3DMode',
        dst: 'Coord3DMode',
        rt_mat: Optional[Union[np.ndarray, Tensor]] = None,
    ) -> Union[Sequence[float], np.ndarray, Tensor, BasePoints]:
        """Convert points from ``src`` mode to ``dst`` mode.

        Args:
            box (Sequence[float] or np.ndarray or Tensor or :obj:`BasePoints`):
                Can be a k-tuple, k-list or an Nxk array/tensor.
            src (:obj:`Coord3DMode`): The source point mode.
            dst (:obj:`Coord3DMode`): The target point mode.
            rt_mat (np.ndarray or Tensor, optional): The rotation and
                translation matrix between different coordinates.
                Defaults to None. The conversion from ``src`` coordinates to
                ``dst`` coordinates usually comes along the change of sensors,
                e.g., from camera to LiDAR. This requires a transformation
                matrix.

        Returns:
            Sequence[float] or np.ndarray or Tensor or :obj:`BasePoints`: The
            converted point of the same type.
        """
        if src == dst:
            return point

        is_numpy = isinstance(point, np.ndarray)
        is_InstancePoints = isinstance(point, BasePoints)
        single_point = isinstance(point, (list, tuple))
        if single_point:
            assert len(point) >= 3, (
                'Coord3DMode.convert takes either a k-tuple/list or '
                'an Nxk array/tensor, where k >= 3')
            arr = torch.tensor(point)[None, :]
        else:
            # avoid modifying the input point
            if is_numpy:
                arr = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(point)).clone()
            elif is_InstancePoints:
                arr = point.tensor.clone()
            else:
                arr = point.clone()

        # convert point from `src` mode to `dst` mode.
        if src == Coord3DMode.LIDAR and dst == Coord3DMode.CAM:
            if rt_mat is None:
                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[0, -1, 0], [0, 0, -1], [1, 0, 0]])
        elif src == Coord3DMode.CAM and dst == Coord3DMode.LIDAR:
            if rt_mat is None:
                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[0, 0, 1], [-1, 0, 0], [0, -1, 0]])
        elif src == Coord3DMode.DEPTH and dst == Coord3DMode.CAM:
            if rt_mat is None:
                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[1, 0, 0], [0, 0, -1], [0, 1, 0]])
        elif src == Coord3DMode.CAM and dst == Coord3DMode.DEPTH:
            if rt_mat is None:
                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1], [0, -1, 0]])
        elif src == Coord3DMode.LIDAR and dst == Coord3DMode.DEPTH:
            if rt_mat is None:
                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[0, -1, 0], [1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1]])
        elif src == Coord3DMode.DEPTH and dst == Coord3DMode.LIDAR:
            if rt_mat is None:
                rt_mat = arr.new_tensor([[0, 1, 0], [-1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1]])
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f'Conversion from Coord3DMode {src} to {dst} '
                'is not supported yet')

        if not isinstance(rt_mat, Tensor):
            rt_mat = arr.new_tensor(rt_mat)
        if rt_mat.size(1) == 4:
            extended_xyz = torch.cat(
                [arr[..., :3], arr.new_ones(arr.size(0), 1)], dim=-1)
            xyz = extended_xyz @ rt_mat.t()
        else:
            xyz = arr[..., :3] @ rt_mat.t()

        remains = arr[..., 3:]
        arr = torch.cat([xyz[..., :3], remains], dim=-1)

        # convert arr to the original type
        original_type = type(point)
        if single_point:
            return original_type(arr.flatten().tolist())
        if is_numpy:
            return arr.numpy()
        elif is_InstancePoints:
            if dst == Coord3DMode.CAM:
                target_type = CameraPoints
            elif dst == Coord3DMode.LIDAR:
                target_type = LiDARPoints
            elif dst == Coord3DMode.DEPTH:
                target_type = DepthPoints
            else:
                raise NotImplementedError(
                    f'Conversion to {dst} through {original_type} '
                    'is not supported yet')
            return target_type(
                arr,
                points_dim=arr.size(-1),
                attribute_dims=point.attribute_dims)
        else:
            return arr

# Copyright (c) OpenMMLab. All rights reserved.
from logging import warning
from typing import Tuple, Union

import numpy as np
import torch
from torch import Tensor

from mmdet3d.utils import array_converter


@array_converter(apply_to=('val', ))
def limit_period(val: Union[np.ndarray, Tensor],
                 offset: float = 0.5,
                 period: float = np.pi) -> Union[np.ndarray, Tensor]:
    """Limit the value into a period for periodic function.

    Args:
        val (np.ndarray or Tensor): The value to be converted.
        offset (float): Offset to set the value range. Defaults to 0.5.
        period (float): Period of the value. Defaults to np.pi.

    Returns:
        np.ndarray or Tensor: Value in the range of
        [-offset * period, (1-offset) * period].
    """
    limited_val = val - torch.floor(val / period + offset) * period
    return limited_val


@array_converter(apply_to=('points', 'angles'))
def rotation_3d_in_axis(
    points: Union[np.ndarray, Tensor],
    angles: Union[np.ndarray, Tensor, float],
    axis: int = 0,
    return_mat: bool = False,
    clockwise: bool = False
) -> Union[Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray], Tuple[Tensor, Tensor], np.ndarray,
           Tensor]:
    """Rotate points by angles according to axis.

    Args:
        points (np.ndarray or Tensor): Points with shape (N, M, 3).
        angles (np.ndarray or Tensor or float): Vector of angles with shape
            (N, ).
        axis (int): The axis to be rotated. Defaults to 0.
        return_mat (bool): Whether or not to return the rotation matrix
            (transposed). Defaults to False.
        clockwise (bool): Whether the rotation is clockwise. Defaults to False.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the axis is not in range [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2], it
            will raise ValueError.

    Returns:
        Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] or Tuple[Tensor, Tensor] or np.ndarray or
        Tensor: Rotated points with shape (N, M, 3) and rotation matrix with
        shape (N, 3, 3).
    """
    batch_free = len(points.shape) == 2
    if batch_free:
        points = points[None]

    if isinstance(angles, float) or len(angles.shape) == 0:
        angles = torch.full(points.shape[:1], angles)

    assert len(points.shape) == 3 and len(angles.shape) == 1 and \
        points.shape[0] == angles.shape[0], 'Incorrect shape of points ' \
        f'angles: {points.shape}, {angles.shape}'

    assert points.shape[-1] in [2, 3], \
        f'Points size should be 2 or 3 instead of {points.shape[-1]}'

    rot_sin = torch.sin(angles)
    rot_cos = torch.cos(angles)
    ones = torch.ones_like(rot_cos)
    zeros = torch.zeros_like(rot_cos)

    if points.shape[-1] == 3:
        if axis == 1 or axis == -2:
            rot_mat_T = torch.stack([
                torch.stack([rot_cos, zeros, -rot_sin]),
                torch.stack([zeros, ones, zeros]),
                torch.stack([rot_sin, zeros, rot_cos])
            ])
        elif axis == 2 or axis == -1:
            rot_mat_T = torch.stack([
                torch.stack([rot_cos, rot_sin, zeros]),
                torch.stack([-rot_sin, rot_cos, zeros]),
                torch.stack([zeros, zeros, ones])
            ])
        elif axis == 0 or axis == -3:
            rot_mat_T = torch.stack([
                torch.stack([ones, zeros, zeros]),
                torch.stack([zeros, rot_cos, rot_sin]),
                torch.stack([zeros, -rot_sin, rot_cos])
            ])
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f'axis should in range [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2], got {axis}')
    else:
        rot_mat_T = torch.stack([
            torch.stack([rot_cos, rot_sin]),
            torch.stack([-rot_sin, rot_cos])
        ])

    if clockwise:
        rot_mat_T = rot_mat_T.transpose(0, 1)

    if points.shape[0] == 0:
        points_new = points
    else:
        points_new = torch.einsum('aij,jka->aik', points, rot_mat_T)

    if batch_free:
        points_new = points_new.squeeze(0)

    if return_mat:
        rot_mat_T = torch.einsum('jka->ajk', rot_mat_T)

    Args:
        coord_type (str): The type of coordinates of points cloud.
            Available options includes:

            - 'LIDAR': Points in LiDAR coordinates.
            - 'DEPTH': Points in depth coordinates, usually for indoor dataset.
            - 'CAMERA': Points in camera coordinates.
        load_dim (int): The dimension of the loaded points. Defaults to 6.
        use_dim (list[int] | int): Which dimensions of the points to use.
            Defaults to [0, 1, 2]. For KITTI dataset, set use_dim=4
            or use_dim=[0, 1, 2, 3] to use the intensity dimension.
        shift_height (bool): Whether to use shifted height. Defaults to False.
        use_color (bool): Whether to use color features. Defaults to False.
        norm_intensity (bool): Whether to normlize the intensity. Defaults to
            False.
        norm_elongation (bool): Whether to normlize the elongation. This is
            usually used in Waymo dataset.Defaults to False.
        backend_args (dict, optional): Arguments to instantiate the
            corresponding backend. Defaults to None.
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 coord_type: str,
                 load_dim: int = 6,
                 use_dim: Union[int, List[int]] = [0, 1, 2],
                 shift_height: bool = False,
                 use_color: bool = False,
                 norm_intensity: bool = False,
                 norm_elongation: bool = False,
                 backend_args: Optional[dict] = None) -> None:
        self.shift_height = shift_height
        self.use_color = use_color
        if isinstance(use_dim, int):
            use_dim = list(range(use_dim))
        assert max(use_dim) < load_dim, \
            f'Expect all used dimensions < {load_dim}, got {use_dim}'
        assert coord_type in ['CAMERA', 'LIDAR', 'DEPTH']

        self.coord_type = coord_type
        self.load_dim = load_dim
        self.use_dim = use_dim
        self.norm_intensity = norm_intensity
        self.norm_elongation = norm_elongation
        self.backend_args = backend_args

    def _load_points(self, pts_filename: str) -> np.ndarray:
        """Private function to load point clouds data.

        Args:
            pts_filename (str): Filename of point clouds data.

        Returns:
            np.ndarray: An array containing point clouds data.
        """
        try:
            pts_bytes = get(pts_filename, backend_args=self.backend_args)
            points = np.frombuffer(pts_bytes, dtype=np.float32)
        except ConnectionError:
            mmengine.check_file_exist(pts_filename)
            if pts_filename.endswith('.npy'):
                points = np.load(pts_filename)
            else:
                points = np.fromfile(pts_filename, dtype=np.float32)

        return points

    def transform(self, results: dict) -> dict:
        """Method to load points data from file.

        Args:
            results (dict): Result dict containing point clouds data.

        Returns:
            dict: The result dict containing the point clouds data.
            Added key and value are described below.

                - points (:obj:`BasePoints`): Point clouds data.
        """
        pts_file_path = results['lidar_points']['lidar_path']
        points = self._load_points(pts_file_path)
        points = points.reshape(-1, self.load_dim)
        points = points[:, self.use_dim]
        if self.norm_intensity:
            assert len(self.use_dim) >= 4, \
                f'When using intensity norm, expect used dimensions >= 4, got {len(self.use_dim)}'  # noqa: E501
            points[:, 3] = np.tanh(points[:, 3])
        if self.norm_elongation:
            assert len(self.use_dim) >= 5, \
                f'When using elongation norm, expect used dimensions >= 5, got {len(self.use_dim)}'  # noqa: E501
            points[:, 4] = np.tanh(points[:, 4])
        attribute_dims = None

        if self.shift_height:
            floor_height = np.percentile(points[:, 2], 0.99)
            height = points[:, 2] - floor_height
            points = np.concatenate(
                [points[:, :3],
                 np.expand_dims(height, 1), points[:, 3:]], 1)
            attribute_dims = dict(height=3)

        if self.use_color:
            assert len(self.use_dim) >= 6
            if attribute_dims is None:
                attribute_dims = dict()
            attribute_dims.update(
                dict(color=[
                    points.shape[1] - 3,
                    points.shape[1] - 2,
                    points.shape[1] - 1,
                ]))

        points_class = get_points_type(self.coord_type)
        points = points_class(
            points, points_dim=points.shape[-1], attribute_dims=attribute_dims)
        results['points'] = points

        return results

@TRANSFORMS.register_module()
class GlobalAlignment(BaseTransform):
    """Apply global alignment to 3D scene points by rotation and translation.

    Args:
        rotation_axis (int): Rotation axis for points and bboxes rotation.

    Note:
        We do not record the applied rotation and translation as in
        GlobalRotScaleTrans. Because usually, we do not need to reverse
        the alignment step.
        For example, ScanNet 3D detection task uses aligned ground-truth
        bounding boxes for evaluation.
    """

    def _check_rot_mat(self, rot_mat: np.ndarray) -> None:

        valid_array = np.zeros(3)
        valid_array[self.rotation_axis] = 1.0

1	# 点云结构:BasePoints 与三个坐标系子类
2	
3	## 1. 本讲目标
4	
5	上一讲(u2-l1)我们搞清了三大坐标系的约定,以及 `Box3DMode` / `Coord3DMode` 这两个转换引擎。本讲把镜头对准点云本身:LiDAR/深度相机吐出来的几十万个三维采样点,在 MMDetection3D 里是如何被表示、变换和转换的。
6	
7	学完本讲,你应该能够:
8	
9	1. 说出 `BasePoints` 的张量布局 \((N, \text{points\_dim})\):前 3 列固定是坐标,其余列通过 `attribute_dims` 登记语义(强度、高度、颜色等)。
10	2. 独立使用 `LiDARPoints` 的 `translate` / `rotate` / `flip` / `scale` 四个刚体变换方法,并解释「为什么只动前 3 列、属性列不动」。
11	3. 解释 `LiDARPoints` / `CameraPoints` / `DepthPoints` 三个子类各自的 `rotation_axis`、`flip` 方向差异,以及 `convert_to` 与 `Coord3DMode.convert_point`、框侧 `new_box` 的配套关系。
12	4. 在数据管线里指出「谁生产了 points 对象、谁在消费它」。
13	
14	> 说明:如果你在旧版资料里见过「points_catdim」之类的说法,请注意当前 1.x 源码中点云对象的维度属性名是 `points_dim`,本讲以源码为准。另外,数据增强里的「平移」操作,点云侧的真实方法名是 `translate`(基类中没有 `shift` 方法),下文不再特别区分这两个词。
15	
16	## 2. 前置知识
17	
18	### 2.1 点云在内存里就是一个二维数组
19	
20	一帧点云就是 N 个采样点,每个点至少有 \((x, y, z)\) 三个坐标,常常还附带:
21	
22	- **强度(intensity)**:激光打到物体表面反射回来的信号强度,KITTI 点云文件每点 4 个 float32,第 4 个就是强度;
23	- **高度(height)**:点到地面的相对高度,室内算法(VoteNet 等)常用;
24	- **颜色(color)**:RGB 三列,来自 RGB-D 相机或带彩色传感器的 LiDAR。
25	
26	所以点云的原始形态就是一个 `(N, D)` 的数组:每行一个点,前 3 列坐标,后面挂属性。**D 可以是 3、4、5、6、7……这正是 `points_dim` 要记录的东西。**
27	
28	### 2.2 刚体变换是什么
29	
30	刚体变换 = 不改变物体形状的几何变换,包括:
31	
32	| 变换 | 数学形式(列向量约定) | 点云增强中的例子 |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| 平移 | \(p' = p + t\) | `RandomShift3D` 随机抖动 |
35	| 旋转 | \(p' = R\,p\) | `GlobalRotScaleTrans` 全局旋转 |
36	| 缩放 | \(p' = s \cdot p\) | `GlobalRotScaleTrans` 全局缩放 |
37	| 翻转(镜像) | 某一坐标分量取负 | `RandomFlip3D` 水平/垂直翻转 |
38	
39	关键点:**旋转和翻转只作用于坐标列;强度、颜色这类属性没有几何意义,不参与变换**。这是本讲反复出现的设计原则。
40	
41	### 2.3 承接上一讲的坐标系结论
42	
43	u2-l1 讲过三套右手坐标系:LiDAR(x 前、y 左、z 上)、CAM(z 前、x 右、y 下)、DEPTH(y 前、x 右、z 上),重力轴分别是 z、y、z。`BasePoints` 的三个子类与之一一对应,子类的全部差异都源于「重力轴是哪根、BEV 平面是哪两根」这两个问题。忘了的话建议先回看 u2-l1 的方向约定图。
44	
45	### 2.4 torch.Tensor 的索引与视图
46	
47	`BasePoints` 内部存的是一个 `torch.float32` 张量,大量使用切片赋值(如 `self.tensor[:, :3] = ...`)和 `clone()`。你需要知道:切片赋值是**原地修改**,`clone()` 是**深拷贝**——这决定了哪些方法会改变点云对象本身(`rotate`、`flip` 都是原地操作),哪些方法返回新对象(`clone`、`to`、`convert_to`)。
48	
49	## 3. 本讲源码地图
50	
51	| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注度 |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| `mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py` | `BasePoints` 基类:张量容器 + 通用变换 + 索引/拼接/搬运 | ⭐⭐⭐ 核心 |
54	| `mmdet3d/structures/points/lidar_points.py` | LiDAR 坐标系子类 | ⭐⭐⭐ 核心 |
55	| `mmdet3d/structures/points/cam_points.py` | CAM 坐标系子类(重写了 `bev`) | ⭐⭐⭐ 核心 |
56	| `mmdet3d/structures/points/depth_points.py` | DEPTH 坐标系子类 | ⭐⭐ |
57	| `mmdet3d/structures/points/__init__.py` | 导出四个类 + `get_points_type` 工厂函数 | ⭐⭐ |
58	| `mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/utils.py` | `rotation_3d_in_axis`:旋转的底层实现 | ⭐⭐ |
59	| `mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/coord_3d_mode.py` | `Coord3DMode.convert_point`:跨坐标系转换引擎 | ⭐⭐⭐ |
60	| `mmdet3d/datasets/transforms/loading.py` | 管线中点云对象的**生产者**(`LoadPointsFromFile`) | ⭐⭐ |
61	| `mmdet3d/datasets/transforms/transforms_3d.py` | 管线中变换方法的**消费者** | ⭐⭐ |
62	| `tests/test_structures/test_points/test_base_points.py` | 官方单测,可当用法示例读 | ⭐ |
63	
64	点云家族与上一讲的框家族(`BaseInstance3DBoxes` + 三子类)完全平行:**基类管通用逻辑,子类只补坐标系相关差异**。两个家族通过同一个 `rotation_3d_in_axis` 工具函数实现「点与框同步旋转」,这是数据增强正确性的根基。
65	
66	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
67	
68	### 4.1 BasePoints:点云张量的统一容器
69	
70	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
71	
72	为什么不让所有代码直接操作裸的 `torch.Tensor`?因为裸张量**只有形状、没有语义**:
73	
74	- 代码无法知道第 4 列是强度还是高度,增强时就不知道哪些列该跟着旋转/缩放;
75	- 代码无法知道这批点在哪个坐标系,`flip`、`bev` 就无法给出正确行为;
76	- 点数可能为 0(空场景)、设备可能在 CPU/GPU 之间搬运,需要统一的封装处理这些边界情况。
77	
78	`BasePoints` 的解决方案是「**张量 + 元数据**」:
79	
80	```text
81	BasePoints 对象
82	├── tensor          (N, points_dim) 的 float32 张量,前 3 列固定是坐标
83	├── points_dim      int,每个点的总维度
84	├── attribute_dims  dict 或 None,登记属性列的语义,如 {'height': 3} 或 {'color': [4,5,6], 'height': 7}
85	└── rotation_axis   int,默认旋转轴(重力轴的列下标),子类中覆盖
86	```
87	
88	一个值得注意的细节:`flip` 和 `convert_to` 虽然标了 `@abstractmethod`,但 `BasePoints` 并没有继承 `ABCMeta`,所以它**仍可直接实例化**——官方单测里就有 `BasePoints(empty_boxes)` 的用法。这个 `@abstractmethod` 更多是「子类必须实现」的文档性约定。
89	
90	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
91	
92	构造一个点云对象的流程:
93	
94	```text
95	输入(Tensor / ndarray / 嵌套列表)
96	    │ torch.as_tensor(..., dtype=float32)      ← 统一类型与设备
97	    ▼
98	若为空张量: reshape 成 (0, points_dim)          ← 空场景是合法输入
99	    ▼
100	断言: dim()==2 且最后一维 == points_dim          ← (N, D) 布局的硬约束
101	    ▼
102	self.tensor = tensor.clone()                    ← 存一份拷贝,与输入解耦
103	    ▼
104	rotation_axis = 0                               ← 基类默认 x 轴,子类会覆盖
105	```
106	
107	#### 4.1.3 源码精读
108	
109	**构造函数与布局断言**:把任意数组输入统一转成 float32 张量,并强制 `(N, points_dim)` 布局;空点云用 `reshape` 而不是新建张量,注释说明是为了不干扰 JIT 追踪。
110	
111	[base_points.py:L33-L54](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py#L33-L54) —— `__init__` 完整流程:类型统一(L41)、空张量处理(L42-45)、形状断言(L46-49)、`clone` 存储(L51)、记录三个元数据(L52-54)。
112	
113	**坐标属性 `coord`**:只读视图返回前 3 列;对应的 setter 允许整体替换坐标列而不动属性列。
114	
115	[base_points.py:L56-L75](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py#L56-L75) —— `coord` property 与 setter,setter 里 `reshape` 失败会抛出清晰的 `ValueError`。
116	
117	**`height` 与 `color`:带「动态生长」的属性访问**。以 `height` 为例:若 `attribute_dims` 里登记过,直接读写对应列;若没登记,**setter 会把张量拓宽一列**(`torch.cat` 追加),并更新 `attribute_dims` 和 `points_dim`。
118	
119	[base_points.py:L77-L111](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py#L77-L111) —— `height` 的 getter/setter;L108-111 就是「追加一列并登记语义」的逻辑。
120	
121	[base_points.py:L113-L150](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py#L113-L150) —— `color` 同理,一次追加 3 列,登记成列表 `[attr_dim, attr_dim+1, attr_dim+2]`(L147-149);setter 还会检查取值范围并告警(L135-136)。
122	
123	**`shape` 与 `bev`**:两个最常被上层代码查询的属性。
124	
125	[base_points.py:L152-L155](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py#L152-L155) —— `shape` 直接透传张量形状。
126	
127	[base_points.py:L256-L259](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py#L256-L259) —— 基类 `bev` 默认取前两列(x-y 平面);下一节会看到 `CameraPoints` 重写了它取 x-z 平面——**同一个属性名,不同子类对应不同的 BEV 平面**。
128	
129	官方单测展示了带属性点云的标准构造方式,值得一读:
130	
131	[test_base_points.py:L26-L71](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/tests/test_structures/test_points/test_base_points.py#L26-L71) —— 构造 7 维点云:`attribute_dims=dict(color=[3, 4, 5], height=6)`,然后断言 `beev/coord/color/height` 各属性切片的正确性。注意 `color` 登记为列表、`height` 登记为单个下标,两种形态都合法。
132	
133	#### 4.1.4 代码实践
134	
135	**实践目标**:亲手构造一个带属性的点云对象,验证张量布局与属性访问。
136	
137	**操作步骤**(示例代码,非项目原有代码,可在装好环境的 Python 交互环境中运行):
138	
139	```python
140	import numpy as np
141	import torch
142	from mmdet3d.structures.points import LiDARPoints
143	
144	# 5 个点:xyz + 第 4 列当强度
145	points_np = np.array([
146	    [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.5],
147	    [0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.5],
148	    [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.5],
149	    [1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.3],
150	    [-1.0, 2.0, 0.5, 0.2],
151	], dtype=np.float32)
152	
153	pts = LiDARPoints(points_np, points_dim=4, attribute_dims=dict(height=3))
154	print(pts.shape)            # torch.Size([5, 4])
155	print(pts.tensor.dtype)     # torch.float32
156	print(pts.coord)            # (5, 3),只有 xyz
157	print(pts.height)           # (5,),第 3 列
158	print(pts.bev)              # (5, 2),前两列
159	print(pts.rotation_axis)    # 2(LiDAR 子类设的,z 轴)
160	```
161	
162	**需要观察的现象**:`coord` 返回的正是 `tensor[:, :3]`;`pts.height` 能取出第 4 列;`bev` 是 x-y 两列。
163	
164	**预期结果**:打印如注释所示。第 4.2 节的变换实践会继续用这个对象。待本地验证。
165	
166	#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案
167	
168	**练习 1**:如果传入 `points_dim=4` 的数组却声明 `points_dim=3`,会发生什么?
169	
170	**答案**:`__init__` 中的断言(`tensor.size(-1) == points_dim`)失败,抛出 `AssertionError`,报错信息会同时给出期望维度和实际形状。这就是 `(N, points_dim)` 布局约束的运行时防线。
171	
172	**练习 2**:对一个 3 维、没有 `attribute_dims` 的点云对象执行 `pts.height = some_values`,对象的 `points_dim` 会变成多少?`attribute_dims` 会怎么变?
173	
174	**答案**:走 setter 的「动态追加」分支(L104-111):张量用 `torch.cat` 拓宽一列,`points_dim` 从 3 变 4,`attribute_dims` 从 `None` 变成 `{'height': 3}`。这个设计允许管线中途补挂属性(比如 `LoadPointsFromFile` 的 `shift_height=True` 场景)。
175	
176	### 4.2 刚体变换四件套:translate / rotate / flip / scale
177	
178	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
179	
180	数据增强(u3-l6 将系统讲解)需要对整帧点云做随机几何扰动,让模型见过更多样的视角与尺度。`BasePoints` 把四种变换都实现为**原地修改**(`in-place`)方法,共同遵守一条铁律:
181	
182	> **只变换 `tensor[:, :3]` 坐标列,`tensor[:, 3:]` 属性列原样保留。**
183	
184	对照基类源码可以逐一验证:
185	
186	- `translate`:坐标列加平移向量,支持 3 维广播或 (N, 3) 逐点平移;
187	- `scale`:坐标列整体乘缩放系数(注意 `height` 属性列**不会**被自动缩放,需要调用方自己处理,见下面的管线代码);
188	- `rotate`:两种输入形态——标量角度(绕 `rotation_axis` 即重力轴转)或直接给 3×3 矩阵;
189	- `flip`:抽象方法,由子类实现,因为「水平翻转翻哪根轴」取决于坐标系。
190	
191	`rotate` 为什么返回旋转矩阵?因为**数据增强必须让点云和 3D 框同步变换**:点转了 θ 角,框除了中心转过去,yaw 也要加 θ。点侧返回的 `rot_mat_T` 会被上游拿去同步处理框(以及 2D 图像标注),这正是 u2-l2 讲过的「点与框用同一个 `rotation_3d_in_axis`」的另一半。
192	
193	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
194	
195	`rotate(rotation, axis=None)` 的执行过程:
196	
197	```text
198	输入 rotation
199	    ├─ numel == 1(标量角度)
200	    │       axis 为 None 时取 self.rotation_axis(重力轴)
201	    │       调 rotation_3d_in_axis(tensor[:, :3], 角度, axis, return_mat=True)
202	    │       写回坐标列,返回 rot_mat_T
203	    └─ shape == (3, 3)(整矩阵)
204	            tensor[:, :3] = tensor[:, :3] @ rotation   ← 行向量右乘
205	            返回该矩阵本身
206	```
207	
208	标量分支的数学:绕 z 轴(`axis=2`,LiDAR/DEPTH 的重力轴)旋转角 \(\theta\),令 \(c=\cos\theta,\ s=\sin\theta\),标准旋转矩阵为
209	
210	\[
211	R_z(\theta)=\begin{bmatrix} c & -s & 0 \\ s & c & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
212	\]
213	
214	源码里 `rotation_3d_in_axis` 实际 stack 出来的是它的**转置** \(R_z(\theta)^{\mathsf T}\),再用 `einsum('aij,jka->aik', points, rot_mat_T)` 做「行向量右乘」。行向量右乘 \(M\) 等价于列向量左乘 \(M^{\mathsf T}\),所以最终效果仍是 \(p' = R_z(\theta)\,p\):
215	
216	\[
217	\begin{bmatrix} x' & y' & z' \end{bmatrix}
218	=
219	\begin{bmatrix} x & y & z \end{bmatrix}
220	\begin{bmatrix} c & s & 0 \\ -s & c & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
221	\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
222	\begin{cases} x' = x\cos\theta - y\sin\theta \\ y' = x\sin\theta + y\cos\theta \\ z' = z \end{cases}
223	\]
224	
225	变量名 `rot_mat_T` 里的 `_T` 就是提醒你「存的是转置形态」。当 \(\theta=\pi/2\) 时简化为 \((x,y,z)\mapsto(-y,\,x,\,z)\),非常适合用来手算验证。

324	
325	**练习 1**:同一行代码 `pts.rotate(np.pi / 4)`,分别作用在 `LiDARPoints` 和 `CameraPoints` 上,旋转轴有什么不同?
326	
327	**答案**:都省略了 `axis` 参数,回落到各自的 `self.rotation_axis`:`LiDARPoints` 是 2(绕 z 轴,在 x-y BEV 平面内旋转),`CameraPoints` 是 1(绕 y 轴,在 x-z BEV 平面内旋转)。两者都是绕重力轴的水平旋转,这正是 BEV 检测任务「旋转增强只改朝向不改俯仰」的需要。

337	### 4.3 三个坐标系子类与 convert_to 跨系转换
338	
339	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
340	
341	三个子类总共只做了三件事,却撑起了全部坐标系语义:
342	
343	1. **设定 `rotation_axis`**:`LiDARPoints` 和 `DepthPoints` 设 2(z 轴),`CameraPoints` 设 1(y 轴)——重力轴不同,默认旋转平面就不同;
344	2. **实现 `flip`**:按 4.2.3 的规律翻转对应列;
345	3. **实现 `convert_to`**:它只是 `Coord3DMode.convert_point` 的语法糖——把自己的坐标系填进 `src`,转发给上一讲讲过的统一转换引擎。`CameraPoints` 额外重写了 `bev`(CAM 的 BEV 平面是 x-z 而不是 x-y)。
346	
347	`convert_to` 转换时会做三件事,与框的转换(`Box3DMode.convert`)严格对应:
348	
349	- **克隆数据**再改,不动原对象;
350	- **前 3 列乘转换矩阵**(支持 3×3 纯旋转,或 3×4 含平移的齐次形式),属性列原样拼接回去;
351	- **用目标坐标系的子类重新包装**,并保留 `points_dim` 与 `attribute_dims`。
352	
353	**与框侧 `new_box` 的配套关系**:框的转换引擎内部用 `BaseInstance3DBoxes.new_box()`([base_box3d.py:L592](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/bbox_3d/base_box3d.py#L592))以同配置创建新坐标系子类实例;点云侧的对应工厂是 `BasePoints.new_point()`([base_points.py:L501-L523](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d/blob/fe25f7a51d36e3702f961e198894580d83c4387b/mmdet3d/structures/points/base_points.py#L501-L523))。而 `convert_point` 里则是直接 `target_type(arr, ...)` 构造目标子类。配套使用的正确姿势:**点云和 3D 框用同一个 `rt_mat` 分别转换,转换后二者仍然对齐**——多模态/可视化代码(MVXNet、lidar2img 投影)都依赖这一性质。
354	
355	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
356	
357	`Coord3DMode.convert_point(point, src, dst, rt_mat)` 的流程:
358	
359	```text
360	src == dst ?  ──是──▶  原样返回
361	    │否
362	克隆输入(裸数组 / BasePoints.tensor 都要克隆,避免改到调用方数据)
363	    ▼
364	rt_mat 未提供? ──是──▶ 查六组坐标系两两默认矩阵(纯轴互换/取负,不含真实标定)
365	    ▼
366	rt_mat 3×4 ? ──是──▶ 坐标列拼 1 变齐次:xyz1 @ rt_matᵀ
367	    └──否(3×3)──▶ xyz @ rt_matᵀ
368	    ▼
369	属性列 arr[..., 3:] 原样拼回:cat([新xyz, remains])
370	    ▼
371	按 dst 选目标子类(CameraPoints / LiDARPoints / DepthPoints)重新包装
372	```
373	
374	注意:六组默认矩阵只做**轴的重排与取负**,描述的是三套坐标系「方向约定」之间的差异;真实传感器之间的转换(LiDAR 装在车上哪个位置、相机外参如何)必须由调用方传入实测的 `rt_mat`(通常来自数据集 info pkl 里的标定矩阵,回顾 u2-l1)。
375	
376	默认 LiDAR→CAM 矩阵可以按方向约定手工推出:CAM 的 x 轴(右)= LiDAR 的 \(-y\),CAM 的 y 轴(下)= LiDAR 的 \(-z\),CAM 的 z 轴(前)= LiDAR 的 \(x\),即
377	
378	\[
379	\begin{bmatrix} x_{cam} \\ y_{cam} \\ z_{cam} \end{bmatrix}
380	=
381	\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}
382	\begin{bmatrix} x_{lidar} \\ y_{lidar} \\ z_{lidar} \end{bmatrix}
383	\]
384	
385	这与源码 L218 行的默认矩阵完全一致。
